# Pagination and "load more"

Google's crawlers do not click buttons, so each page in a series needs its own URL and a normal `<a href>` link to the next. Google's pagination guide says later pages should not use page 1 as their canonical. On Day 2 Google said on stage that pointing paginated pages' canonical to page 1 can sometimes make sense, for example to make a category page more visible, but that it affects canonicalization and deduplication; this contradicts Day 1 and is not in Google's docs, and a 2013 Google post says the content of the later pages would then not be indexed at all. For infinite scroll, Google has said it renders with a very tall viewport that can miss content, and its lazy-loading guide asks for paginated loading with a unique URL per chunk. Moving to infinite scroll or a load-more button was called risky, depending on what you want to achieve, because Googlebot does not click buttons. In the Day 1 Q&A, captured by a second recording, Google answered a question about replacing thousands of paginated category pages with a JavaScript load-more button: without crawlable links to the further pages, Google will not see them at all.

Based on: `D1-C115`, `D2-C393`, `D2-C395`, `D2-C200`, `D2-C276`, `D1-C114`, `D2-C394`, `D2-C203`, `D1-C491`.

## What to do

- Keep self-referencing canonicals on paginated pages; point them to page 1 only if you deliberately want later pages folded in and their items are linked from elsewhere.
- Give every page or loaded chunk its own URL, linked with `<a href>`, including behind infinite scroll and 'load more'.
- Treat a switch to infinite scroll or 'load more' as risky: plan crawlable links to every page before launch.

## What Google's documentation says

- **[Docs]** Google's crawlers do not click buttons. Each page in a series needs its own URL and an `<a href>` link to the next page, should not use page 1 as its canonical, and rel=next and rel=prev are no longer used.
  <br><sub>`D1-C115` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · is the documentation · [Pagination, incremental page loading, and their impact on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/ecommerce/pagination-and-incremental-page-loading) · Repeated by [D2-C040](../sessions/D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) · Extended by [D2-C184](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C187](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C195](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C201](../sessions/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C268](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C276](../sessions/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) · Contradicted by [D2-C393](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C395](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-06`</sub>

- **[Docs]** In Google's March 2023 SEO office hours, John Mueller said Google handles infinite scroll with viewport expansion, rendering a page like a very long phone, which is not very efficient and can miss content, so pagination links are strongly recommended.
  > "this is done through a technique called "viewport expansion", where we render a page like a very long phone."
  <br><sub>`D2-C200` · Google Search Central (SEO office hours transcript, March 2023) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session D: Rendering and JavaScript · is the documentation · [March 2023 Google SEO office hours](https://developers.google.com/search/help/office-hours/2023/march)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's 2013 post on rel=canonical mistakes says pointing rel=canonical from page 2 or later of a paginated series to page 1 is incorrect because the pages are not duplicates, and that it would result in the content on later pages not being indexed at all.
  <br><sub>`D2-C395` · Search Central blog (8 April 2013) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [5 common mistakes with rel=canonical](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2013/04/5-common-mistakes-with-relcanonical) · Extends [D1-C115](../sessions/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-06`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's pagination guide says the pages of a paginated sequence may share the same title and description, and suggests linking every page of the sequence back to the first page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C832` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · is the documentation · [Pagination, incremental page loading, and their impact on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/ecommerce/pagination-and-incremental-page-loading) · Used by `DEV-URL-06`</sub>

## Analysis

- **[Analysis]** Audit tabs, accordions and 'load more' lists for content fetched on click or scroll: put tab content in the initial DOM and hide it with CSS, trigger lazy loading with an Intersection Observer, and give long lists paginated URLs linked with `<a href>`.
  <br><sub>`D2-C203` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session D: Rendering and JavaScript</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's pagination guide still says not to use page 1 as the canonical of a paginated series, so keep self-referencing canonicals on paginated pages unless you deliberately want later pages folded into page 1 and the items they list are linked from elsewhere.
  <br><sub>`D2-C394` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Handling web duplication · [Pagination, incremental page loading, and their impact on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/ecommerce/pagination-and-incremental-page-loading) · Used by `DEV-URL-06`</sub>
